sentences.text: In this episode I will guide you through some useful expressions for buying tickets, asking about the movie, finding your seat, talking during and after the movie, and much more.
I'm going to speak slowly and clearly so don't worry.
Buying tickets at the cinema.
When you arrive at the cinema the first thing you need to do is buy your tickets.
Let's go over the key phrases you'll need for that.
Common phrases.
Hi, I would like to buy a ticket for the movie.
What time does the movie start?
How much is a ticket?
Is there a student discount?
Can I buy tickets online?
Do you have any tickets for the evening show?
Are there any available seats for the 5 p.m.
show?
I would like one adult ticket for the Lion King.
Hi, I'd like to buy one ticket for the Lion King please.
Sure, what time would you like to go?
What time is the next showing?
The next show is at 5 p.m.
I'll take one for the 5 p.m.
show please.
Tip, if you want to buy something extra like popcorn or a drink, don't forget to ask the staff.
You can say, can I also get a large popcorn and a Coke please?
Do you have any ice cream?
Can I have some water?
Two, asking about the movie.
Before you buy your ticket, you might want to know more about the movie you're going to see.
Here are some useful questions for asking about the movie.
Common phrases.
What is the movie about?
Is this movie good?
Is this movie suitable for children?
Is this a comedy or a drama?
How long is the movie?
Who are the main actors in this movie?
What genre is the movie?
Is the movie in English or dubbed?
Example Can you tell me what this movie is about?
It's a family friendly movie about a group of animals who go on an adventure.
That sounds fun.
How long is the movie?
It's one hour and 45 minutes long.
Tip, if you don't know what genre you like, asking about the genre can help you choose the right movie.
You can say, what type of movie is this?
Is it an action movie or a thriller?
Finding your seat.
After you buy your ticket, you need to go into the cinema and find your seat.
You might need help from the staff or need to ask for directions.
Common phrases.
Where is my seat?
Is this seat taken?
I'm looking for seat number five.
Can I sit in the front row?
Which row is the best?
Do you have any seat number?
Here is seat ten.
Seat ten is in the middle row.
Go straight and turn left.
Thank you.
If you're confused about where to sit, don't hesitate to ask the cinema staff for directions.
They are always happy to help.
It's important to remember that you should be quiet during the movie.
But before or after the movie, here are some useful things you might want to say.
Common phrases.
This is a great movie.
I love this actor.
The special effects are amazing.
I don't understand the plot.
This scene is so exciting.
Can you believe what just happened?
Example dialogue.
Wow, the special effects are amazing.
Yes, the action scenes are incredible.
I can't wait to see how it ends.
Tip.
If you need to ask someone a question during the movie, whisper so you don't disturb other people.
You can ask something like, what's happening now?
Or what did he just say?
Five.
Talking about the movie afterward.
Once the movie ends, you can talk with your friends or other people about what you watched.
Common phrases.
What did you think of the movie?
I really liked it.
The ending was amazing.
I think the movie was too long.
It was a bit boring in the middle.
The plot was interesting, but the ending was confusing.
Example dialogue.
So what did you think of the movie?
I loved it.
The actors were great.
I agree.
The ending was a little sad, but still amazing.
Yes, I didn't expect that twist.
Tip.
Sharing your opinions after the movie is a fun way to practice your English.
You can talk about the acting, the plot, the special effects, and more.
Six.
Small talk before or after the movie.
While you're waiting for the movie to start or after it's finished, you can make some small talk with your friends or people around you.
Here are some phrases for casual conversations at the cinema.
Common phrases.
Have you seen this movie before?
What other movies do you like?
What's your favorite genre?
How often do you go to the cinema?
Have you been to the cinema before?
Example dialogue.
Hi.
Have you seen this movie before?
Yes, I saw it last week.
It's one of my favorites.
That's awesome.
I'm excited to see it for the first time.
I'm sure you'll love it.
Tip.
Small talk is a great way to practice English in a relaxed setting.
If you meet someone new, you can talk about the movie or ask them about their favorite films.
Cinema etiquette.
When you're at the cinema, it's important to follow some basic rules and be respectful to others.
This helps everyone have a good time.
Key etiquette tips.
Arrive on time.
Try to get there early so you don't miss the beginning of the movie.
Turn off your phone.
Make sure your phone is off or on silent so it doesn't disturb others.
Don't talk loudly.
During the movie, try to keep your conversation short and quiet.
No photos or videos.
Don't take pictures or videos during the movie.
It's usually not allowed.
Keep your feet off the seats.
Don't put your feet on the back of the seat in front of you.
If you really enjoyed the movie, feel free to clap at the end to show your appreciation.
And that's all for today's episode.
Now you know how to speak English at the cinema.
Whether you're buying tickets, asking about the movie, or talking to your friends afterward.
I hope you're feeling confident about going to the movies in English.
